faq.q: What kind of homes are over $1.8M in Langley?
faq.a: On the first page read: acreage estates — equestrian properties with barns and arenas in Campbell Valley, large new-build estates in Salmon River, a 39.5-acre multi-building estate in Otter District, and Brookswood parcels carrying coach houses and plan-area potential. The page's own copy also frames Willoughby executive homes and Fort Langley heritage properties as part of the segment, but neither appeared on the first page.

faq.q: Can an over-$1.8M Langley acreage add another home?
faq.a: It depends on the parcel's ALR status and zone, not on the price band. On ALR land, the ALC frame allows one principal residence up to 500 m² plus at most one additional detached residence of 90 m² (parcels 40 ha or less) or 186 m² (over 40 ha), with a suite only inside the principal residence; Township SSMUH does not rescue larger lots — eligibility ends at 4,050 m² on serviced Urban Containment Boundary land.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house to a house in Langley?
faq.a: BC's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow more homes on many urban lots, but each municipality sets the details and many lots are excluded. Check the lot's zoning with the municipality before you plan a suite or coach house.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in Langley?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.
